title: Fallen Angel pattern definition
claim: Stocks that gap up significantly then sell off heavily but reverse during the first 2 hours exhibit higher win rates due to false breakdown and covering dynamics
support: Author describes gap-up reversal as core Fallen Angel strategy in Ch6. Stock gaps up overnight, opens higher, sells off to support, then reverses back up.
mechanism: Gap-up euphoria attracts profit-taking; stock consolidates at support; covering and retail demand drive reversal
assumptions: Gap up is catalyst-driven, not earnings disaster
Stock has sufficient float and volume
failure_modes: Gap reversal doesn't hold; continues lower
Support level breaks; stock extends down

title: ABCD pattern recognition
claim: ABCD patterns on 5-min charts using Fibonacci ratios (0.618 AB=CD) indicate likely reversal points at D
support: Author provides ABCD pattern framework with Fibonacci targets
mechanism: Fibonacci ratios align with supply/demand equilibrium

title: Bull flag consolidation breakouts
claim: Bull flags in strong uptrends with volume confirmation (150%+ of average) breakout with higher frequency than random consolidations
support: Author discusses bull flag pattern and volume confirmation
mechanism: Consolidation provides equilibrium; volume confirms breakout

title: Opening Range Breakout (ORB) strategy
claim: Early breakouts (within first 2 hours) from opening range show higher win rates than later-day breakouts
support: Author emphasizes ORB as core early-day pattern
mechanism: Gap indicates institutional catalyst; early breakout shows momentum continuation
assumptions: Market is liquid enough for early fills

title: VWAP bounce strategy with candlestick confirmation
claim: VWAP bounces in uptrends with bullish candlestick confirmation (engulfing, hammer) have win rate > 55%
support: Author describes VWAP strategy with confirmation filters
mechanism: VWAP is institutional cost basis; mean reversion common; candlestick reduces noise

title: Candlestick pattern validation for entries
claim: Bullish candlestick patterns serve as secondary confirmation filters, reducing false signals when combined with technical setups
support: Author uses candlestick patterns as confirmation for entry filters
mechanism: Candlestick body/wick structure reflects intra-bar price action and sentiment

title: Position sizing formula based on account and stop distance
claim: Pre-calculated position size = (Account * Risk_%) / Stop_Distance; sizing before entry prevents over-leverage
support: Author emphasizes fixed-fractional sizing as core risk management
mechanism: Ties risk to actual stop distance; reduces account risk per trade
assumptions: Stop distance can be estimated pre-entry

title: Consecutive loss limit as ruin protection
claim: Enforce max 2-3 consecutive losses before stopping; exceeding indicates strategy is out of sync
support: Author emphasizes consecutive loss limits as ruin protection rule
mechanism: Consecutive losses signal regime change; more losses increase ruin probability exponentially

title: Daily loss limit enforcement
claim: Maximum daily loss should not exceed 2-3% of account; exceeding triggers automatic trading halt
support: Author describes daily loss limits as essential circuit breaker
mechanism: Daily limit prevents cascading losses; preserves capital for recovery

title: Risk percentage varies by strategy and market regime
claim: Risk per trade should be 1-3% depending on strategy win rate, market volatility, and trader experience
support: Author recommends risk scaling to expected outcome and volatility
mechanism: Higher win-rate strategies tolerate higher risk; volatility impacts sizing

title: No overnight holds rule to avoid gap risk
claim: All intraday positions closed before EOD (3:30 PM ET) to eliminate overnight gap exposure
support: Author forbids overnight holds due to gap and margin risk
mechanism: Overnight gaps (earnings, geopolitics) can move stock 5-20%; intraday focus avoids multi-day risk

title: Level 2 market data for order book pattern recognition
claim: Real-time Level 2 (bid/ask depth) data is critical for detecting order book walls and reversal probability
support: Author emphasizes L2 data access as requirement for order book strategy
mechanism: Shallow bid/ask indicates fakeout; deep orders show institutional intent
assumptions: L2 data is available from broker

title: Pre-market session insights for gap analysis
claim: Pre-market trading (4:00 AM - 9:30 AM) reveals overnight news and institutional pre-positioning
support: Author uses pre-market data for gap-based strategies like Fallen Angel
mechanism: Pre-market is lower-volume, wider spreads; large moves often retrace intraday

title: Execution latency impact on slippage
claim: Order round-trip latency > 100ms on short-term patterns results in adverse fills; optimal is < 50ms
support: Author emphasizes execution quality as alpha driver for short-term strategies
mechanism: Intraday prices move ticks in milliseconds; latency causes slippage

title: Float and market cap filtering for watchlist generation
claim: Stocks with float < 50M shares and market cap customizable exhibit stronger intraday moves
support: Author uses float filters for stock selection in watchlist
mechanism: Low-float stocks have higher volatility; small order imbalances cause larger moves

title: Transaction cost attribution for true PnL calculation
claim: Commission, slippage, bid-ask spread, and market impact must be tracked per trade; gross PnL minus costs = net PnL
support: Author stresses importance of accurate transaction cost accounting
mechanism: Small-edge strategies are profitable only if transaction costs are minimized

title: Execution quality is alpha generator for short-term strategies
claim: For strategies with small edge (1-5% win rate advantage), execution quality dominates; 5-tick improvement compounds to 2-5% return difference annually
support: Inferred from author emphasis on latency, slippage, and execution precision
mechanism: Latency, fills, liquidity access are leverage multipliers for small edges

title: Adaptive risk sizing based on market regime detection
claim: Platform should detect market volatility regimes (calm, normal, stressed) and adjust position sizing accordingly to maintain consistent risk-adjusted returns
support: Author mentions risk % varies by market condition; system automation can enhance this
mechanism: VIX or ATR-based regime detection allows dynamic sizing without trader intervention
